claim: When a tool door gains new error reason codes, extend every closed reason vocabulary between it and the model in the same change, because a relay that normalizes unrecognized reasons back to unknown erases the protocol-vs-handler distinction the codes were added for.
because: lens-scan execute r-20261014192943-c5dd: a page-bridge fix coded unknown_tool/invalid_arguments/tool_error at the inject door, but the gate and the desktop relay map any reason outside their closed list to unknown, so a re-judge still found the two error channels indistinguishable and the change was reverted.

claim: When a CLI transport port gains an out-of-band result channel (exit code, stderr tail) beside its streamed lines, pin it with a test that spawns a real child through the production transport, because a scripted fake reports the channel by construction and the real adapter can keep reporting the default unnoticed.
because: scan-sweep challenge 2026-10-15: an exit handle and a stderr reader landed with 8 green acceptance cases, all on the scripted transport; the subprocess transport never called report(), so every real run read exit 0 until a real-child test (2 cases red before) drove the fix.

claim: When a host writes a child's input before it reads the child's exit, write it inside the scope that reaps the child and treat a closed or reset pipe as no error, because a child that refuses at startup exits unread and a large input then turns its classified exit and stderr into an unreaped broken-pipe exception.
because: athena-portable 3ef59b4: a 4 MiB stdin to a child that exits 2 without reading raised BrokenPipeError (WinError 109) out of the transport, skipping ADR 0109's exit classification and leaving the child unreaped; after the fix the exit code and stderr tail are reported. No subprocess-lifecycle technique mentions stdin or a broken pipe.

claim: When a canvas or camera binds its keyboard handler on the container, decline any key that is already defaultPrevented, carries Ctrl/Meta/Alt, or targets an editable descendant, because the container hears every key typed inside it and otherwise eats text input, double-handles a child's roving key and swallows the browser's page zoom.
because: cab6dd1: probe showed '-' typed in a field zoomed the camera and never reached the field, a roving list's arrow also orbited, Ctrl+= was prevented; an atlas surface had already worked around it with `event.target !== canvas`

claim: When an overlay's focus restore is deferred to a later frame, resolve the fallback target (and the invoker's connectivity) inside that frame, not at teardown, because the surface beneath can rebuild the landmark between teardown and restore and a teardown-time lookup answers nothing.
because: 26f8424: probe with the origin card re-created by an effect of the closing commit dropped focus to the body; resolving in the frame focused the card

claim: When a state attribute or class toggles a property in CSS, declare the transition on the base selector and let the state rules set values only, because a transition runs on the after-change style, so one declared only on the hidden state animates the exit and pops the enter (and one on a child never fires when the state sets the parent's opacity).
because: atlas lanes: the detail tiers' transition sat only under [data-band=0] and the run's on .al-run-line while data-dim set .al-run; a stylesheet test reading rules (comments stripped) went red on both and green after moving the transitions

claim: When model text that passed through a JSON decoder is written to a UTF-8 file, pipe or child's stdin, encode it with an escaping error handler, because a model's half-emoji escape decodes to a lone surrogate that no UTF-8 sink accepts, and a strict encode then fails at the write - typically the final report, after the spend.
because: athena-portable 01260f8: a judge reason holding '\ud83d' (shape-checked only) made a Gauntlet run raise UnicodeEncodeError in write_report after every call was paid, leaving a cut report.json and no report.md; backslashreplace reads back as the same JSON string. No structured-output or eval technique mentions surrogates or the write side of decoded model text.

claim: When the shell mounts a fresh view for every navigation (a keyed layer, a route element), a test of state that must survive a round trip unmounts and remounts the view between steps, because re-rendering one root keeps component state the running app discards.
because: athena-portable chores: wired and intake tests re-rendered one root and passed while the stage dropped the catalogue's filters, the topic's scroll and the front door's opening message on every move; remounting in the tests turned 5 red, a module store turned them green, and Edge probes confirmed both sides.

claim: When an activity log lets any reversible entry be undone in any order, make each inverse a compare-and-set against the value its write produced and refuse (rolling back the whole undo, with the reason) when a later write owns the field, because a blind inverse silently overwrites newer work and leaves the newer write's record counted as live.
because: tidycrm: tidy a company then settle the domain, undo the tidy - the blind inverse put the pre-tidy value back over the settled name and the settle's revision still counted in the export summary; a compare-and-set on new_value plus a refusal fixed it (70d7708)

claim: When a lint-style checker exempts a literal (an alpha stop, a marker), strip the exempt literal from the line and still test the rest, because a per-line exemption lets any violation that shares the line pass with it.
because: hirelane's check-law exempted whole lines naming box-shadow/mask-image or holding one white plane; seeded `box-shadow: ... #e11d48` passed until the literals were stripped instead (ea206f1).

claim: When a test file's scratch fixture is reaped by a file-level after hook that also restores process state (working directory, env), prove at each use that the resource resolved is the scratch copy, because the runner may fire that hook as soon as the tests declared so far drain, and a cwd-resolved handle then silently re-opens the live one.
because: node:test ran tempHome's root after() between two test() calls separated by a top-level await; later tests wrote 95 rows to the dev server's SQLite file over eight runs; a books() assertion on cwd and db().file caught the seeded repeat

claim: When a list mixes items from a source whose read failed with items that do not depend on that source, keep the independent items under a distinct failure line instead of hiding them, because the list must agree with what the system will actually use.
because: lens-scan pack k-des-1: the Origins tab of a desktop companion appended shell-run generic tools to a page's failed tool read; the approved fix said to hide them, but they are sent with every turn, so hiding them would have traded one false claim for another.

claim: When consent to a tool server is granted per origin, record a canonical hash of each tool's name, description, schema and flags at consent and re-gate any tool whose hash later differs, because a payload-free change notification lets a trusted server rewrite a description into an injection that inherits standing approval.
because: athena-portable desktop re-listed WebMCP tools on toolchange with no diff (a recorded mcp-tools deviation); the landed fix (5c0b5d2, ADR 0100) re-gates a description-only edit and was verified by a 5-scenario store test.

claim: In a Tauri 2 shell, declare rename_all on every command (or none) and test one invoke per command shape, because Tauri maps command arguments to camelCase by default and a snake_case caller fails at IPC while a catch-all error path hides it.
because: athena-portable's hands_call alone lacked rename_all = snake_case while the panel sent tab_id, so every generic hand and card capture would fail in the live shell and the capture path swallowed it as no picture; fixed in 2d16183.

claim: When an agent's runs across several app tabs must be gathered into one durable case, stamp each turn id under the case and join receipts by turn id rather than routing the tabs into one shared conversation, because a shared conversation carries every tab's history into every turn.
because: tiger 2026-10-22 on athena-portable: routing a case's tabs into one conversation cost 1.7-2.5x per bench run on 5 playbooks and pushed a 14-portal run over its $8 cap (short 4/12, baseline exceeds 3 of 3); turn stamps (ADR 0127) keep the conversation byte-identical, held by a test.

claim: When a recurring agent job resumes, do not put a list of the previous run's approved actions into the prompt as carry-forward; inform at the approval card with a dated 'you approved this exact call on <date>' line instead, because a listed action reads to the model as work to do again.
because: tiger 2026-10-22 on athena-portable: a 'since last run' prompt block raised re-filed duplicates of run-1 items from 6 to 14 across 5 playbooks (n=1 per arm, paid two-run bench); the block was removed (ADR 0130) and the gate-side dated line kept.

claim: When a catalog item carries both an authored value estimate and a measured example, derive the headline from the measured answer key, tag every figure with its kind (money back, protected, penalty avoided, count), and let only one kind sum into totals, because untyped dollar figures from weights, exposure and released payments silently inflate every aggregate.
because: athena chores UAT: 94/100 authored values disagreed with their own test worlds and 39-66% of an area's found total was not money; after deriving and typing, number-honesty criteria went 2 to 14 of 28 on the same pairs

claim: When a paired peer reaches a local agent through an HTTPS reverse proxy on the same host (e.g. an overlay provider serve feature), do not rely on the peer-address class gate, because every proxied request arrives from the host itself and passes it; either keep the listener on the overlay address directly or move admission to the proxy identity header.
because: one-athena-fleet WP4 analysed tailscale serve in front of an overlay-only listener and found it would launder all traffic past the classifier; the feature was declined and the listener stays bound to the overlay IP

claim: When an agent runtime executes tool calls in the client window rather than the server, route remote control (phone, peer device) as a message into that window composer, not as remote per-call hands, because the window owns timeout and unsure semantics and the gate stays single.
because: one-athena-fleet found host calls are client-driven (window posts tool_results back); a remote composer reused the whole gate path and needed one tee instead of a cross-network run loop

claim: When a companion's one global turn lock is split into per-thread locks, audit every object the turn path shares across threads for per-turn fields (deadlines, feedback sets, last-result slots) and make them per-turn or thread-local, because the global lock was silently serialising that state and the split turns a correct design into a wall-clock race.
because: athena-portable fleet-surfaces: RoundHarness kept _deadline and _told on the shared instance; with two conversations running, a later turn start reset the earlier turn's 25-minute wall and mixed their told-sets; fixed with threading.local and a two-thread test.

claim: When a companion's background cycle does its heavy work remotely (a cloud model leg) and only a small local child runs here, do not let a sustained host-CPU hold starve it: hold on the resource the local part actually consumes (memory) and let the staleness release outrank a CPU hold, because a developer workstation can sit at 90-100% CPU for hours from unrelated work and the cycle then never runs.
because: device-vitals smoke: the stdlib CPU probe matched Windows' own counter (100/93/88 vs 98/100/100) on a PC saturated by docker, launchers and other agent sessions; a forced sleep cycle was held 'CPU at 100%' on two of three runs while its local child weighed ~330 MB of 64 GB.

claim: When the agent's turns carry live machine telemetry (load, free slots, queue state), tell the consolidation pass that such readings are re-measured every turn and are not facts, because the distiller otherwise writes the reading it saw in a transcript as a durable belief.
because: A real compress leg distilled 'PC has ... 3 background task slots' from an answer to a room question; one added prompt line removed it while the four durable facts and the procedure were still written (n=1 each side).

claim: When a consuming host validates a tool catalogue as a whole (one bad schema refuses every tool), test each of the host's acceptance rules producer-side and post the real manifest to the real host once at the seam, because the failure is total and invisible from the producer's side.
because: Shadowrunr console exposed to Athena, 2026-10-23: the first scripted seam run found the whole 27-tool manifest refused because array params lacked maxItems (HostManifest.validate); no console unit test could see it; fixed with a per-property maxItems test.

claim: When a host packs tool listings into a bounded prompt block with a greedy prefix cut in a fixed order, measure each publisher's footprint with a port of the host's own line renderer and hold it to a share of the bound, because the cut drops the first entry that does not fit and every entry after it, orientation tools included.
because: Athena's 12,000-char capability block, GATED/READ/AUTO then name: a 28-tool catalogue at 8,099 chars lost where_am_i (40 of 41 entries listed); cut to 25 tools and 4,801 chars with a 5,000 budget test; the port reproduced 4,801 exactly on the listed tools (2026-10-24).

claim: When the host's tool listing renders only top-level parameter types, restate every constraint nested inside an array's items (legal values, which records accept the write) in the description, because the schema still enforces it but the model never sees it and fails validation guessing.
because: Athena renders an array param as 'tags: array'; leave_feedback failed validator_failed in a live pilot until its description named the 8 legal tags (2026-10-23); a catalogue check then found add_tone_line naming 3 of its 12 legal tags, which the producer tests had passed (2026-10-24).

claim: When a consumer hard-caps each tool result, design every result to fit a guard below the cap at realistic fixture size, page long documents with an outline and a next offset, and trim lists with a footer that also drops any cursor that would skip the trimmed items, because the consumer's cut is silent, lands mid-JSON, and the agent then asks the human for the content.
because: Athena cuts host results at 1,600 chars: a 13.9k-char document read came back truncated and she asked the operator to paste it; after paging (1,200-char pages, outline, next_offset, a 1,500 guard tested per tool at largest inputs) she filed the edit card and it was approved (live pilot runs 1 and 2, 2026-10-23, n=1).

claim: When an agent edits a long document through an approval card, expose find/replace against the base digest of the newest read, with exactly one match required and a stale digest refused, rather than a whole-document write, because the person approves a readable change and the write cannot clobber a concurrent edit.
because: Shadowrunr edit_character_doc (2026-10-23): card filed, approved, package validated, backup named in the live pilot; on the real desktop the approved card changed exactly before.replace(find, find + added).

claim: When trust in a tool producer is keyed to each tool's contract hash, give the pairing procedure an explicit re-grant step after the producer's tools are listed, and repeat it after any tool change, because tools that registered after the grant all ask for approval, reads included, and the pairing looks broken.
because: Athena ADR 0100: registering the console's origin while its opt-in was off accepted no contracts, so every tool asked once on the real desktop until Origins Disable/Enable (2026-10-23); the guide gained the step and the e2e driver a retrust command.

claim: When an agent-facing tool surface is tuned, run a fixed live pilot with a per-case report (calls before the first content-bearing call, cards, unknown tools, cost) before and after each fix wave, because it turns a transcript diagnosis into a measured comparison and shows which fixes moved nothing.
because: Shadowrunr x Athena pilot, 4 cases: total $5.66 to $4.22, start_sim from 4 failed calls to 1, a walkthrough from 12 calls to 7, a shaping case from no card to an approved edit (n=1 per case, 2026-10-23).

claim: When automating a Tauri (WebView2) dev build over CDP, attach with a page-level raw CDP transport (one socket per page target from /json/list) instead of a browser-level attach, because a blob shared worker reported without browserContextId makes Playwright's connectOverCDP assert inside an event handler and kill the process uncatchably.
because: Playwright 1.63 and 1.64 against Athena's dev build (UI from Vite): the process died on attach; athena-portable drive/raw-cdp.mjs ran the 6-test desktop suite 6/6 in attach mode (2026-10-23).

claim: When an e2e launches an isolated build of a desktop app, rebuild it from a clean tree immediately before each use into its own target directory, because the binary embeds whatever frontend dist the working tree held at build time and another session's uncommitted UI ships inside it.
because: Athena's isolated e2e exe built at 23:05 embedded another session's uncommitted companion UI that the driver could not open; a rebuild from the clean tree into a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR fixed it (2026-10-24).

claim: When an e2e drives a user's own long-lived agent instance, expect its cost to grow every run because the persistent conversation is re-read on each turn, and use an isolated instance for repeated runs, because clearing the panel does not clear the agent's session.
because: The same 6 desktop tests: $5.68 attached to the operator's Athena against $1.38 on an isolated launch (2026-10-23); her Clear empties only the panel.

claim: When a suite defaults a sibling checkout to <repo root>/../<name>, resolve it through the main checkout (git rev-parse --git-common-dir) or require it explicitly, and fail when zero tests ran, because from a linked worktree the default points nowhere and every test skips with exit 0.
because: athena-portable test:e2e:shadowrunr run from .claude/worktrees/open-skill: 13 of 13 skipped ('no shadowrunr binary at ...worktrees/overlord'), exit 0; with SHADOWRUNR_ROOT set, 8 passed (2026-10-24).

claim: When an agent works an app through published tools, count every fallback to generic page reading or clicking as a missing-tool finding, and number lines and items in tool results exactly as the page numbers them, because the agent fills the gap by scraping and its references then disagree with the API's.
because: Athena character audit 2026-10-24: no tool returned a show's pick reasons, so she used page_read, whose line numbers were offset by about 12 from the API's.

claim: When an agent analyses a dataset through bounded tools, pair each of its sampled claims with a deterministic script over the full data before the result is published, because bounded reads make it sample, and sampled claims are confirmed, corrected or extended at full scale.
because: Athena audited a character over 8 turns and 68 calls ($18.29) from ~25-line samples; a script over all 260 runs confirmed a gag in 140 of 260, corrected a poll cadence (about 88 s, not 150) and added humor-landed rates by tier (2026-10-24).

claim: When an app is driven by an agent, never let a landing, intro or route-restore navigation replace a route already set, and open the app with its target route, because the agent's navigation a moment after load is silently undone.
because: Shadowrunr console: the intro navigated with replace after Athena had moved the console; only the live driver exposed it; fixed in overlord f694b9d (2026-10-23).

claim: When an id is unique only inside a container, either require the qualified form or make the refusal list the candidates and say how to qualify, because bare ambiguous ids cost the agent failed calls.
because: Athena character audit 2026-10-24: a bare run id present in two tournaments cost a failed call; the error said how to qualify it and she recovered on the next call.

claim: When a scope column is added to a memory index that recall ranks by importance, put the ranking column in the scope index (scope, kind, importance) so the count and top-k queries stay index-only, because a (scope, kind) index forces a table read per lane.
because: projects-layer memory wall: recall over 5,000 nodes went +10-12% with (space, kind) and +2.7% median with (space, kind, importance); episode count 0.09 ms -> 1.7 ms -> back to index-only.
